pairs.source_text: Dictatore habente comitia Caesare consules creantur Iulius Caesar et P. Servilius: is enim erat annus, quo per leges ei consulem fieri liceret.
pairs.question: Quis fuit collega Caesaris in consulatu eo anno, quo Pompeium acie in Thessalia superavit?
pairs.question_en: Who was Caesar's colleague in the consulship in the year in which he defeated Pompey in battle in Thessaly?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Caesar and his consulship of 48 BC (the year of Pharsalus); single named answer supported verbatim by 'consules creantur Iulius Caesar et P. Servilius'. Caesar's colleague P. Servilius Isauricus is closed-book history; the Thessaly anchor fixes the year.

pairs.source_text: Eo legiones XII, equitatum omnem venire iusserat. Sed tantum navium repperit, ut anguste XV milia legionariorum militum, DC equites transportari possent.
pairs.question: Quot fere legionarios milites et quot equites Caesar primo transitu ex Brundisio in Graeciam transportare potuit?
pairs.answer: Quindecim milia militum et sescentos equites.
pairs.question_en: About how many legionary soldiers and how many cavalry could Caesar transport in his first crossing from Brundisium to Greece?
pairs.answer_en: Fifteen thousand soldiers and six hundred cavalry.
pairs.derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and the crossing of the Adriatic from Brundisium; the figures (XV milia, DC) are supported verbatim by 'XV milia legionariorum militum, DC equites transportari possent'. Caesar's shortage of ships for the bold winter crossing is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Praeerat Aegyptiis navibus Pompeius filius, Asiaticis D. Laelius et C. Triarius, Syriacis C. Cassius, Rhodiis C. Marcellus cum C. Coponio, Liburnicae atque Achaicae classi Scribonius Libo et M. Octavius. Toti tamen officio maritimo M. Bibulus praepositus cuncta administrabat; ad hunc summa imperii respiciebat.
pairs.question: Quis toti officio maritimo Pompeianae partis praepositus erat, penes quem summa imperii navalis erat?
pairs.question_en: Who was placed in charge of all naval affairs on Pompey's side, with whom rested the supreme command of the fleet?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Pompey's fleet; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Toti tamen officio maritimo M. Bibulus praepositus cuncta administrabat; ad hunc summa imperii respiciebat'. M. Bibulus, Caesar's old consular colleague, as Pompey's fleet commander is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Sed cum prope Dyrrachium Pompeius constitisset castraque metari iussisset, perterrito etiam tum exercitu princeps Labienus procedit iuratque se eum non deserturum eundemque casum subiturum, quemcumque ei fortuna tribuisset.
pairs.question: Apud utrum imperatorem, Caesarem an Pompeium, T. Labienus bello civili stetit?
pairs.question_en: On which commander's side, Caesar's or Pompey's, did Titus Labienus stand in the civil war?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to T. Labienus, Caesar's chief legate in Gaul; that he had gone over to Pompey is supported by his swearing never to desert him ('se eum non deserturum'). Labienus' defection to Pompey is iconic and closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Erant enim circum castra Pompei permulti editi atque asperi colles. Hos primum praesidiis tenuit castellaque ibi communit. Inde, ut loci cuiusque natura ferebat, ex castello in castellum perducta munitione circumvallare Pompeium instituit.
pairs.question: Quem ducem Caesar apud Dyrrachium continuatis munitionibus circumvallare instituit?
pairs.question_en: Which commander did Caesar undertake to encircle with continuous fortifications at Dyrrachium?
pairs.derivation: Operation fact anchored to Caesar and Dyrrachium; single named answer supported verbatim by 'circumvallare Pompeium instituit'. The lines of Dyrrachium, where Caesar blockaded Pompey, are closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Pompeius eo proelio imperator est appellatus. Hoc nomen obtinuit atque ita se postea salutari passus est, sed neque in litteris scribere est solitus, neque in fascibus insignia laureae praetulit.
pairs.question: Quo nomine Pompeius post proelium ad Dyrrachium, ubi Caesarem reppulit, ab exercitu suo appellatus est?
pairs.question_en: By what name was Pompey hailed by his army after the battle at Dyrrachium, where he repulsed Caesar?
pairs.derivation: Title fact anchored to Pompey and the battle at Dyrrachium; supported verbatim by 'Pompeius eo proelio imperator est appellatus' (eo proelio = the Dyrrachium engagement). Caesar's repulse at Dyrrachium and Pompey's acclamation as imperator are closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Pompeius, iam cum intra vallum nostri versarentur, equum nactus, detractis insignibus imperatoris, decumana porta se ex castris eiecit protinusque equo citato Larisam contendit.
pairs.question: In quod Thessaliae oppidum Pompeius statim ex castris victus profugit, postquam acie a Caesare superatus est?
pairs.question_en: To which town of Thessaly did the defeated Pompey flee straight from his camp after he was beaten in battle by Caesar?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Pompey and his defeat by Caesar (Pharsalus, in Thessaly); single named answer supported verbatim by 'equo citato Larisam contendit'. Pompey's immediate flight to Larisa after Pharsalus is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: In eo proelio non amplius CC milites desideravit, sed centuriones, fortes viros, circiter XXX amisit.
pairs.question: Quot fere milites Caesar in proelio, quo Pompeium in Thessalia devicit, amisisse se scribit?
pairs.question_en: About how many soldiers does Caesar say he lost in the battle in which he decisively defeated Pompey in Thessaly?
pairs.derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and the battle that defeated Pompey (Pharsalus); supported verbatim by 'non amplius CC milites desideravit'. The famously light Caesarian losses at Pharsalus are closed-book; eo proelio = the Pharsalus battle, supplied by the question.

pairs.source_text: Ex Pompeiano exercitu circiter milia XV cecidisse videbantur, sed in deditionem venerunt amplius milia XXIIII.
pairs.question: Quot fere milia hominum ex Pompei exercitu in proelio Thessalico cecidisse Caesar tradit?
pairs.question_en: About how many thousands of men from Pompey's army does Caesar report fell in the Thessalian (Pharsalus) battle?
pairs.derivation: Number fact self-anchored to Pompey's army; supported verbatim by 'Ex Pompeiano exercitu circiter milia XV cecidisse videbantur'. The lopsided casualties at Pharsalus (against Caesar's ~200) are closed-book; indirect statement 'cecidisse ... tradit'.

pairs.source_text: Ibi casu rex erat Ptolomaeus, puer aetate, magnis copiis cum sorore Cleopatra bellum gerens, quam paucis ante mensibus per suos propinquos atque amicos regno expulerat.
pairs.question: Quis Aegypti rex erat, cum Pompeius profugus eo pervenit?
pairs.question_en: Who was king of Egypt when the fugitive Pompey arrived there?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Egypt and Pompey's arrival; supported verbatim by 'rex erat Ptolomaeus, puer aetate'. The boy-king Ptolemy (XIII) at the time of Pompey's death is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Ibi casu rex erat Ptolomaeus, puer aetate, magnis copiis cum sorore Cleopatra bellum gerens, quam paucis ante mensibus per suos propinquos atque amicos regno expulerat.
pairs.question: Cum qua sorore, quam regno expulerat, Ptolomaeus rex Aegypti eo tempore bellum gerebat?
pairs.question_en: With which sister, whom he had driven from the kingdom, was Ptolemy, king of Egypt, then at war?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Ptolemy, king of Egypt; supported verbatim by 'cum sorore Cleopatra bellum gerens, quam ... regno expulerat'. The war between Ptolemy and his sister Cleopatra is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Ipsi clam consilio inito Achillam, praefectum regium, singulari hominem audacia, et L. Septimium, tribunum militum, ad interficiendum Pompeium miserunt. Ab his liberaliter ipse appellatus et quadam notitia Septimii productus, quod bello praedonum apud eum ordinem duxerat, naviculam parvulam conscendit cum paucis suis: ibi ab Achilla et Septimio interficitur.
pairs.question: A quibus duobus viris Pompeius in Aegyptum profugus interfectus est?
pairs.question_en: By which two men was Pompey killed when he had fled to Egypt?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Pompey and Egypt; the two killers are supported verbatim ('Achillam, praefectum regium ... et L. Septimium, tribunum militum, ad interficiendum Pompeium miserunt ... ab Achilla et Septimio interficitur'). Pompey's murder on arrival in Egypt is iconic and closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Alexandriae de Pompei morte cognoscit atque ibi primum e nave egrediens clamorem militum audit, quos rex in oppido praesidii causa reliquerat.
pairs.question: In quo Aegypti oppido Caesar, Pompeium persecutus, de eius morte cognovit?
pairs.question_en: In which Egyptian city did Caesar, having pursued Pompey, learn of his death?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Caesar and Pompey; single answer supported verbatim by 'Alexandriae de Pompei morte cognoscit'. Caesar's arrival at Alexandria, where he learned of Pompey's murder, is closed-book and opens the Alexandrian war.
